newsitem.title: USA: Varlen to meet/exceed '97 EPS concensus.
newsitem.headline: Varlen to meet/exceed '97 EPS concensus.

text.p: Varlen Corp, after reporting stronger than anticipatedd first quarter results Thursday, said it expects its results for the year to at least match the current consensus of analysts' earnings forecasts.
"I feel confident that we can meet or exceed analysts estimates," Richard Wellek, president, said in a telephone interview.
Wellek based his outlook on the current First Call mean estimate for 1997, which is $2.25 a share compared with $2.04 a year ago.

Varlen reported higher earnings for the first quarter of $0.63 a share, compared with $0.60 a year ago, beating analysts' projections of lower quarterly results. The First Call consensus for the quarter was $0.53 a share.
"The strength came in truck and rail," Wellek said.
Varlen shares Thursday morning were up 1/2 at 24-1/8.
Wellek said that, in spite of heavy-duty truck industry sales that declined three percent, Varlen's business rose 16 percent due to gains in market share and increased content per vehicle.
He said the outlook for Varlen's heavy-duty truck business is good, based on the increased content and industry projections that truck sales in 1997 will be flat to up five percent compared to 1996.
In rail, Varlen saw a pick up in demand for components used in locomotives, railcars and track maintenance late in the first quarter.
"We see it sustaining at least through the second quarter," Wellek said.

Varlen's analytical products business, which includes quality control instruments for the petroleum refining industry, faces a tough comparison in the first half of 1997 due to the sale last July of a non-core business.
Based on orders, however, Wellek said this business should have a stronger second-half than the prior year.
